subject: DONE s393c (d50a326): global partition reads a Unicode package name — one shared $ID regex; mro utf8 rows repaid
description:
FOUND s392 by #304's companion-suite audit (the snapshot staleness had hidden it).
LIVE, load-time CRASH.  Not a coverage-loss judgment call — the file dies.

REPRODUCER (12 lines, dies under PCL, prints "ok" under perl):
    use utf8;
    use strict; use warnings;
    {
        { package Ascii; our @ISA = ('X'); }
        { package બʑ;    our @ISA = ('X'); }
    }
    print "ok\n";
  → `Cannot proclaim a macro variable special: બʑ::@ISA`

EMISSION (the whole diagnosis is in three lines):
    (p-defcell Ascii::@ISA (make-array 0 …))     <- ordinary partition
    (defvar    બʑ::@ISA    (make-array 0 …))     <- EXCEPTION partition  ← wrong

ROOT CAUSE — `Pl/GlobalPartition.pm::_split_name`, the qualified-name arm:
    elsif ($rest =~ s/^([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::[A-Za-z_]\w*)*):://) { $pkg = $1 }
The FIRST character of each segment is matched ASCII-only (`[A-Za-z_]`), while
`\w` afterwards matches unicode.  So `Baɾ::` splits fine (ASCII `B`) and
`બʑ::` does not — _split_name returns (), which partition_name reads as "not
word-shaped" = cause (a) = EXCEPTION = `defvar`.

WHY IT CRASHES RATHER THAN MERELY DIVERGING: `p-defpackage`
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:439) ensures `@isa` storage for EVERY package it defines,
so `@ISA` is ALREADY a symbol-macro cell when the emitted `defvar` runs.  That
is exactly the hazard GlobalPartition's own header comment names ("declaring a
name defvar (special) and then also define-symbol-macro'ing it is a load-time
error in SBCL").  Ordinary globals other than @ISA do NOT crash — both
emitters ask the same (wrong) partition and agree — but they silently keep the
pre-Direction-D defvar model, so the `local` lowering and the my-shadow rule
answer for a class the flip was supposed to have emptied.

SHAPE-DEPENDENT, which is why it survived the gate: the declaration must be
emitted QUALIFIED.  `package બʑ { our @ISA = … }` at file top level emits an
UNQUALIFIED `(p-defcell @ISA …)` and is fine; the nested-block shape above (and
t/mro/*_utf8.t) emits `બʑ::@ISA`.

COST MEASURED (s392 suite run vs snapshot): mro/next_edgecases_utf8.t 9 → 0
rows (XDIFF → DIFF, no TAP at all), mro/basic_utf8.t 10 → 9 (XDIFF → DIFF).
Other utf8 mro files are already XDIFF-registered, so they hide it.

FIX SHAPE: one regex — accept the same character set the emitter PRODUCES for
a package segment (unicode word chars, first char not a digit), i.e. the
`[A-Za-z_]` classes become the unicode-aware equivalent in BOTH the segment
head and the pipe-quoted arm's neighbours.  Do NOT special-case @ISA.
VERIFY: this is the partition function — every emitted global goes through it,
so a widening moves names exception → ordinary.  Bar = corpus-diff (expect
IDENTICAL: no corpus file has a non-ASCII package name) + gate + FULL SWEEP
(TOTAL/LOST), plus a guard row in Pl/t/global-partition-01.t (which already
pins the three name tables' coincidence) and the reproducer above as a run row.
Re-run t/mro/*_utf8.t afterwards and move the two files' rows.
